corrections.note: When first listed, Theorem 2.2 and Proposition 3.2 were shown under ARR-2026-5XEX8EX0629R997Y. The citing paper attributes them to its reference [8], ARR-2026-4FYHCBAQ0T8FHRBT, and cites ARR-2026-5XEX8EX0629R997Y separately as reference [7]. Both citations are now listed as printed.

cites.reference: L. Eriksson, Euler-reduced Tjurina floors for osculating-absorbing Gauss fibres, Preprint ARR-2026-5XEX8EX0629R997Y, version 2 (2026), Version record.
cites.use: Named as giving the same lower bound for arbitrary isolated plane germs.
cites.summary: After stating its plane minimum, formula (30), equivalently ⌊(3m² − 2m − 4)/4⌋, the citing paper notes that the AIRR record describes an Euler-reduced generator count giving the same lower bound for arbitrary isolated plane germs. It names no numbered statement of the record.

check.detail: Theorem 3.1 of version 2 states τ(h) ≥ ⌊(3s² + 4s − 3)/4⌋ for every isolated plane curve germ of order at least s + 1. With m = s + 1 this is ⌊(3m² − 2m − 4)/4⌋, the value printed in the citing paper.

cites.reference: [L. Eriksson], Prescribed Tjurina algebras and complete spectra in osculating-absorbing Gauss fibres, Preprint ARR-2026-4FYHCBAQ0T8FHRBT, version 1 (2026), https://arr-research.github.io/papers/ARR-2026-4FYHCBAQ0T8FHRBT/.
cites.location: Section 1.3, “Relation to earlier work”, and Section 6.3, “Surface singularities”
cites.use: Its three-variable minimum is recovered as a case of the citing paper’s formula (31).
cites.summary: The AIRR record is credited with a lower bound for the Tjurina number over all isolated three-variable germs of prescribed multiplicity, and with the explicit one-term polynomial xᵐ + yᵐ + zᵐ + (x + y + z)ᵐ⁺¹ that attains it. The citing paper states that its formula (31) recovers this three-variable minimum as a case of its theorem in arbitrary dimension.

check.detail: Theorem 2.2 of version 1 is the bound τ(h) ≥ s(s + 2)(2s − 1)/3 for isolated three-variable germs of order at least s + 1, and Proposition 3.2 is equality for xˢ⁺¹ + yˢ⁺¹ + zˢ⁺¹ + (x + y + z)ˢ⁺². With m = s + 1 the polynomial is the one printed in the citing paper, and its formula (31), (m − 1)³ − 2·C(m − 1, 3), equals s(s + 2)(2s − 1)/3.
